title: No unwritten tradition equals Scripture — sole rule of faith
source_text: XXXVI. Unde patet nullam esse traditionem non scriptam, quae authoritate comparari debeat cum scriptis divinis & Apostolicis: adeoque Scripturam esse unicam fidei regulam, cui alia non possit adjungi quae vim eandem habeat obligandi conscientiam, & fidem obstringendi. Ac proinde, si ipsa sufficiens non esset, neque omnia, quae ad fidem pertinent, contineret, sequeretur Ecclesiam ejusmodi regula sufficienti carere, nec illius saluti sufficienter fuisse provisum.
pass_a_gloss: Whence it is plain that there is no unwritten tradition which ought to be compared in authority with the divine and Apostolic writings: and therefore that Scripture is the unique rule of faith, to which another cannot be joined that has the same force of binding the conscience and constraining faith. And accordingly, if it itself were not sufficient, and did not contain all things which pertain to faith, it would follow that the Church lacked a sufficient rule of that kind, and that provision had not been sufficiently made for her salvation.
pass_b_english: So there is no unwritten tradition that should be matched in authority with the divine and Apostolic writings.

Scripture is the sole rule of faith; nothing else can be joined to it with the same power to bind conscience and constrain faith. If Scripture were not enough and did not hold all that belongs to faith, the Church would lack a sufficient rule, and her salvation would not have been adequately provided for.

choices.why: Exclusive rule claim vs dual-source Roman view.
Authority parity denied, not all notice of custom.
